comparison: Both strongly support the identification and characterization of ancyromonad ChRs (C3-C5, C29-C35). OpenEval emphasizes bioinformatics, phylogenetic analysis, and sequence alignment methods. Peer reviewers affirm this as a key contribution, noting phylogenetic placement and database scanning without methodological concerns.

Both support ion selectivity findings (C6-C7, C41-C43, C62-C63, C65, C68). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of ion substitution experiments with statistical analysis. Peer reviewers acknowledge the identification of two anion-conducting and one cation-conducting ChR without questioning the methods.

Both support NlCCR's superior performance compared to PsChR2 (C8, C58). OpenEval notes statistical significance and appropriate comparison methodology. Peer reviewers emphasize the opsins are 'uncommonly fast, potent' and note high-quality experimental data.

Both support spectral characterization (C39-C40). OpenEval evaluates patch clamp recordings and action spectra (C39-C43). Peer reviewers praise 'thorough characterization of biophysical properties' including spectral properties (C39-C40, C51), though peer review groups fewer claims together.

Perfect agreement on spectral separation for multiplexed optogenetics (C53-C54). Both support co-expression experiments demonstrating bidirectional photocurrent responses. OpenEval notes FRET as technical artifact; peer reviewers emphasize relevance for multicolor applications.

Both support photocycle kinetics findings (C69-C72, C75-C76, C78). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of flash photolysis and transient absorption data. Peer reviewers note 'valuable insights into molecular mechanism' and emphasize 'extraordinarily fast onset kinetics.'

Both support pH titration and D226N mutant findings (C81-C88). OpenEval emphasizes correspondence between pH-induced and mutant spectral shifts as strong evidence. Peer reviewers acknowledge mutagenesis revealed roles of key residues affecting spectral and kinetic properties.

Both support G86E mutant characterization (C92-C95, C99-C102). OpenEval details correlation between M-like intermediate and proton transfer mechanism. Peer reviewers note this contributes to 'valuable insights into molecular mechanism' and mechanistic principles.

Both support paradoxical mutational effects (C108-C109, C111-C113, C115, C119, C159). OpenEval emphasizes unexpected results suggesting different retinal pocket geometry. Peer reviewers acknowledge these findings as part of mechanistic insights without challenge.

Both support color-tuning residue identification (C124-C126). OpenEval evaluates mutagenesis showing blue-shifting effects. Peer reviewers explicitly state mutagenesis 'revealed roles of key residues in photoactive site affecting spectral properties.'

Both support two-photon excitation capability (C9, C131-C134, C136). OpenEval confirms two-photon absorption via quadratic power dependence. Peer reviewers explicitly note AnsACR is 'useable in multiphoton experiments' at commonly used wavelengths.

Both support brain slice validation (C10, C137-C140, C167). OpenEval details action potential suppression and notes axonal depolarization effects. Peer reviewers state the study 'validated functionality in mouse brain slices' and note ability to 'silence neuronal activity.'

Both support C. elegans pharyngeal pumping inhibition (C11, C141-C144, C146-C147, C150). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of EPG recordings with statistical analysis. Peer reviewers state the study 'validated functionality in vivo in C. elegans, demonstrating versatility.'

Both support light intensity dependence characterization (C55-C56). OpenEval notes saturation kinetics and desensitization patterns, though finds 'complex light dependence' interpretation vague. Peer reviewers include this as part of 'thorough characterization' without specific concerns.

Both support ion selectivity methods (C59-C61, C64). OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive ion substitution experiments with automated and manual patch clamp. Peer reviewers specifically praise 'modern automated patch-clamp approaches' as a strength.

Both support NlCCR kinetic characterization (C79-C80). OpenEval notes single exponential kinetics distinguishing NlCCR from ancyromonad ACRs. Peer reviewers include this as part of kinetic characterization described as 'uncommonly fast.'

Both support Q48E mutant findings (C107). OpenEval evaluates functional effects on channel kinetics. Peer reviewers include this as part of mutagenesis work that 'revealed roles of key residues in photoactive site.'

Both support high pKa and photostability findings (C104-C105). OpenEval notes simultaneous spectral parameter changes and calls photostability link speculative but supported. Peer reviewers include this as contributing to 'valuable insights into molecular mechanism.'

Both support color-tuning mutagenesis including negative results (C129-C130). OpenEval notes lack of reciprocal effects in AnsACR suggests context-dependent mechanisms. Peer reviewers acknowledge these unexpected results support conclusions about different binding pocket geometry.

Both support evolutionary and functional interpretations (C154-C155, C157-C158). OpenEval notes unpredictability of ion selectivity and NlCCR as good optogenetic tool. Peer reviewers state work provides 'valuable insights' and expands understanding of 'opsin biophysics in general.'

Both support conclusion about optogenetic utility (C175). OpenEval calls this forward-looking, acknowledging need for further evaluation. Peer reviewers directly support this, stating work 'demonstrated versatility' and ChRs 'expand the optogenetics toolkit.'

OpenEval evaluates protein purification and spectroscopic measurements (C50-C52), noting quantitative yield data and spectral discrepancy explanation. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though spectral characterization is generally praised.

OpenEval evaluates evolutionary inferences about early ChR acquisition (C151-C153). Notes speculation depends on phylogeny accuracy. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though evolutionary context is acknowledged.

OpenEval evaluates paradoxical spectral tuning mechanisms (C159-C165), noting lack of structural data limits understanding and calls for structural studies. Peer reviewers acknowledge paradox generally but no specific evaluation of these mechanistic speculation claims.

OpenEval evaluates axonal activation concerns and trafficking motif speculation (C166-C168). Notes C168 is speculative future work representing limitation. Peer review R12 mentions C167 but doesn't specifically evaluate trafficking motif speculation.

OpenEval evaluates contextual comparison with previous C. elegans work (C169-C171), noting mechanistic explanation based on channel vs pump efficiency. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates established knowledge about C. elegans pharyngeal anatomy (C172-C174), noting this contextualizes but doesn't represent new findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
